posts.summary:

The post The imec Report: Advancing The CFET-Based Device Roadmap appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The semiconductor industry is transitioning from FinFETs to GAA nanosheet transistors, which enable 5.5-track standard cells for the A10 logic generation.
Complementary FET (CFET) architectures, which stack p and nMOS transistors vertically, are being developed to scale standard cells down to 3T and extend the CMOS roadmap to the A3 node.

Imec is evaluating two primary manufacturing paths for CFETs: monolithic (mCFET), which processes the structure in a single sequence, and sequential (sCFET), which patterns top and bottom devices independently.
The shift toward CFETs and CMOS 2.0 heterogeneous integration is driven by the need to meet the diverse, high-performance requirements of AI-centric applications.

bullets: Northeastern University researchers introduced 'ROBBIN,' a hardware-aware attack that leverages Rowhammer-induced bit-flips to inject backdoors into AI models during inference.
Unlike previous methods that treat bit-flips as side effects, ROBBIN characterizes specific DRAM vulnerabilities to strategically map model weights to susceptible memory pages.
This approach creates highly robust backdoors that maintain high attack success rates (ASR) while preserving the target accuracy (TA) of the model across different hardware devices.
The research underscores a critical security vulnerability in AI deployment, as it demonstrates that hardware-level memory manipulation can compromise model integrity even after deployment.

bullets: Researchers at the University of Alberta developed 'PPAPlace,' a differentiable surrogate model that predicts post-route timing metrics directly from macro and standard-cell placements.
The study highlights that traditional HPWL-based optimization correlates poorly with final timing, leading to PPA degradation in existing AI-driven placement tools.
By utilizing post-global-routing labels, the model achieved a 22% improvement in worst negative slack (WNS) and a 51% improvement in total negative slack (TNS) on benchmark circuits.
The PPAPlace framework integrates into existing analytical placers as a co-objective or a refinement step, offering a path to better silicon performance without requiring retraining for new circuits.

posts.title: Autonomy and Innovation
posts.summary: Incentives favor offense when it comes to agentic cybersecurity; it's the same dynamic that will limit incumbents and fuel startups in the long run.
bullets: The distinction between 'white hat' and 'black hat' hackers is defined by intent and incentives rather than technical capability, as both groups utilize the same fundamental skillsets to exploit or patch vulnerabilities.
In the context of AI, the proliferation of powerful, widely available models means that cybersecurity threats are no longer restricted to a single entity or nation-state.

Attempting to restrict access to advanced AI models is a flawed strategy because the best defense against AI-driven cyberattacks requires that defenders have equal or superior access to the same powerful models.

The author argues that government-led efforts to centralize AI control, such as the response to Anthropic's Fable release, are counterproductive and ignore the reality of a decentralized, global AI landscape.

posts.title: Issues Stack Up With More HBM Layers
posts.summary:
Hot Chips 2026: Thinner dies, more TSV area, thermal dissipation, and limited manufacturing capacity make HBM scaling much more difficult.
The post Issues Stack Up With More HBM Layers appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Increasing HBM layer counts to meet AI bandwidth demands is creating significant manufacturing hurdles, including die warpage and structural defects from thinning.
Higher stack heights increase power density and thermal resistance, complicating heat dissipation from the base logic die.
Through-silicon vias (TSVs) essential for bandwidth consume valuable die area, reducing storage capacity per layer and lowering overall manufacturing yields.
HBM production is becoming increasingly inefficient in terms of silicon and wafer capacity per bit compared to conventional DRAM, leading to higher costs and potential supply constraints.

posts.title: From GAA To CFET: Scaling Transistors For The AI Era

bullets: The transition from Gate-All-Around (GAA) to Complementary FET (CFET) architectures is essential for maintaining transistor scaling density in the AI era.
Backside power delivery networks are becoming a critical enabler for new transistor structures, allowing for improved power efficiency and reduced signal interference.
Design Technology Co-Optimization (DTCO) is increasingly vital to ensure that new transistor geometries can be effectively integrated into high-performance AI accelerator designs.
These structural advancements are necessary to overcome the physical limitations of current FinFET and early GAA nodes as power density requirements continue to climb.

The actual effects of AI on the labor market still seem shrouded in deep uncertainty. When it comes to predictions on near-term impacts, we can see two camps emerge. A deep bench of established and renowned labor economists continues to expect “small” effect sizes, at least by the standards of the drastic predictions common in San Francisco. The creators of the technology, most prominently Anthropic’s CEO, Dario Amodei, predict widespread displacement and high unemployment. If there is absorption of the displaced, it will be into worse jobs that might not even be around for long. On that view, AI is markedly abnormal: while past technologies have complemented distinctly human contributions, such as intelligence or creativity, AI is sufficiently broad and general that we should expect it to exceed and supplant these human contributions to the economy, leaving human workers largely obsolete...

bullets: Labor economists remain divided on AI's impact, with some predicting productivity-driven job growth while others, including industry leaders like Anthropic’s CEO, warn of widespread human obsolescence.
The core debate centers on whether AI will act as a complement to human labor or as a general-purpose technology capable of supplanting human intelligence and creativity entirely.
